mainTopic: The סוטה's מנחה, and the step-by-step order of bringing a regular מנחה, with a source for each stage
overview: The amud opens by finishing a proof about the סוטה. According to the view that she drinks before her מנחה is offered, the scroll is already erased, so tiring her out cannot be about saving the scroll. Next the גמרא quotes our משנה, which says every מנחה is in a כלי שרת from start to finish. It challenges this from a ברייתא in which the owner brings his מנחה from home in silver and gold baskets. רב פפא answers that the משנה means vessels fit to become a כלי שרת. The גמרא shows that even רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who allows wooden service vessels, would reject a cheap basket. The גמרא then goes through the ברייתא line by line and gives a source or reason for each stage: placing the מנחה in a כלי שרת, oil and לבונה, bringing it to the כהן and to the southwest corner of the מזבח, moving the לבונה aside, taking the קומץ from the oily spot, a second קידוש like blood, and gathering the לבונה. The amud ends in the middle of the ברייתא, as the כהן brings the קומץ up.

steps.title: The scroll is already erased, so the reason must be different
steps.stepSummary: According to the view that the סוטה drinks first and her מנחה is offered afterward, the scroll is already erased by the time of the מנחה. So tiring her out with the מנחה cannot be meant to protect the scroll.
steps.simpleTranslation: [According to the view that] he gives her the water to drink and afterward offers her מנחה: if [the tiring out] were because of the scroll, the scroll has already been erased!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a proof that started before this part of the daf. It shows that the reason for tiring out the סוטה is not to save the מגילה from being erased.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One idea was that the כהן tires her out so she will confess, so that the מגילה with ה׳'s name will not be erased. But according to the view that she drinks before the מנחה is offered, the מגילה was already erased in the water before that point. So the tiring must have a different purpose: the תורה is looking out for her.

keyTerms.meaning: he gives her (the סוטה water) to drink
the scroll with the curses, including ה׳'s name, that is erased into the water

steps.whatToRemember: According to the view that the סוטה drinks first, the מגילה is already erased before the מנחה is offered. So the tiring out cannot be about protecting the scroll.

phrases.english: he gives her to drink, and afterward
he offers her meal-offering.
So if it were because of the scroll,
phrases.notes: He means: if the reason for tiring her out were to keep the scroll from being erased.

phrases.english: it has already been erased!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי מִשּׁוּם מְגִילָּה הָא אִימְּחִיקָא לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a proof begun in the earlier part of the daf.
steps.raayaObject: That tiring out the סוטה is not meant to protect the scroll from being erased.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The view that the סוטה drinks before her מנחה is offered.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to contradict the משנה about service vessels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה, which says all מנחות are in a כלי שרת from start to finish. It then brings a ברייתא where the owner first carries his מנחה from home in ordinary silver and gold baskets.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] 'All meal-offerings, etc.' And they raised a contradiction: What is the order of meal-offerings? A person brings a meal-offering from his house in baskets of silver and gold. He puts it into a service vessel, sanctifies it in the service vessel, and puts its oil and frankincense on it. Then he carries it to the כהן. The כהן carries it to the altar and brings it near the southwest corner, opposite the point of the corner, and that is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes our משנה and then begins quoting a ברייתא that seems to contradict it. Step 6 gives the answer to this contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says a מנחה is in a כלי שרת from the very beginning. But the ברייתא says the owner first brings it in ordinary baskets of silver and gold, and only later puts it into a כלי שרת. So the two sources seem to disagree about whether the מנחה always has to be in a holy vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: and they raised a contradiction (between two sources)
a holy vessel used for the service in the בית המקדש
bringing the מנחה near to the altar (from מַגִּישָׁהּ)
the southwest corner of the altar

steps.confusionAlert: The contradiction is only about the first stage, the baskets from home. Everything after that in the ברייתא does use a כלי שרת.

phrases.english: All meal-offerings, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה: every מנחה is in a כלי שרת from beginning to end.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
The order of meal-offerings, how is it done?
A person brings a meal-offering from his house
in baskets of silver and of gold,
phrases.notes: These are ordinary baskets, not holy vessels. That is the part that clashes with the משנה.

phrases.english: and he puts it into a service vessel,
and sanctifies it in the service vessel,
and puts its oil and frankincense on it,
and carries it to the priest.
And the priest carries it to the altar,
and brings it near at the southwest corner
opposite the point of the corner,
and that is enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that every מנחה is in a כלי שרת from beginning to end.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא has the owner bring the מנחה from home in ordinary silver and gold baskets before it goes into a כלי שרת.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: taking the handful and burning it
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues the order of the מנחה. The כהן moves the frankincense aside and takes a handful (קמיצה) from the oily part. He sanctifies it in a כלי שרת, puts the frankincense on top, brings it up the altar, salts it, and burns it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He moves the frankincense to one side. He takes a handful from the place where most of its oil is, puts it into a service vessel, and sanctifies it in the service vessel. He gathers its frankincense and puts it on top of the handful, and brings it up to the altar. He brings it up and burns it in the service vessel, salts it, and puts it on the fires.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the same ברייתא it brought for the contradiction. This part describes the קמיצה and the burning on the altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these stages uses a כלי שרת, just as the משנה says. So the conflict is still only about the first stage, when the מנחה is brought from home in baskets.

keyTerms.meaning: takes a handful (the קמיצה) from the מנחה

phrases.english: And he moves the frankincense to one side,
and takes a handful from the place where its oil is most plentiful,
and puts it into a service vessel,
and sanctifies it in the service vessel.

phrases.aramaic: וּמְלַקֵּט אֶת לְבוֹנָתָהּ וְנוֹתְנָהּ עַל גַּבָּיו,
phrases.english: And he gathers its frankincense and puts it on top of it,
and brings it up to the altar,
and brings it up and burns it in the service vessel,
and salts it, and puts it on the fires.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the ברייתא brought for the contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule about כלי שרת from beginning to end.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is the same ברייתא as the previous step; this part simply finishes the order of the service.

steps.title: The ברייתא ends: what the כהנים may do with the leftovers
steps.stepSummary: Once the handful is offered, the rest of the מנחה is eaten. The כהנים may add wine, oil, and honey to it. The only thing forbidden is letting it become חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once the handful has been offered, the leftovers are eaten. The כהנים are allowed to put wine, oil, and honey into it. They are forbidden only from letting it become leavened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא. This last part is about the שיריים, the leftover part of the מנחה. Step 5 states the challenge, and Step 6 answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the קומץ is offered, the כהנים may eat the rest. They may even add honey, although honey may not be offered on the altar. The one rule they must keep is that the leftovers cannot become חמץ.

keyTerms.meaning: its leftovers, the part of the מנחה left after the handful is taken

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא lays out the full order of a מנחה. Only its first stage, bringing the מנחה from home in silver and gold baskets, seems to clash with our משנה. The גמרא will now resolve that clash.

phrases.english: Once the handful has been offered, its leftovers are eaten,
and the priests are allowed to put into it
wine, oil, and honey,
and they are forbidden only from letting it become leavened.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes quoting the ברייתא brought for the contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule about כלי שרת from beginning to end.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is the end of the same ברייתא; the contradiction itself rests on the baskets in step 2.

steps.title: The challenge: the ברייתא says silver and gold baskets
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states its challenge outright. The ברייתא says the owner brings his מנחה in ordinary silver and gold baskets, but the משנה says all מנחות are in a כלי שרת from beginning to end.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the ברייתא teaches that the owner brings it in silver baskets and gold baskets!
steps.whatsHappening: After quoting the long ברייתא in Steps 2-4, the גמרא now points to the one detail that causes the problem: the silver and gold baskets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says all other מנחות are in a כלי שרת from start to finish. But the ברייתא says the owner first brings his מנחה from home in his own silver and gold baskets, which are not service vessels. So the two sources seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, it teaches (used to point to the key detail in a quoted source)

steps.confusionAlert: Most of the long ברייתא in Steps 2-4 is not the problem. The only part that causes the difficulty is the silver and gold baskets at the very beginning.

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches
phrases.notes: "It" is the ברייתא quoted in Steps 2-4.

phrases.aramaic: בִּקְלָתוֹת שֶׁל כֶּסֶף וּבִקְלָתוֹת שֶׁל זָהָב!
phrases.english: in baskets of silver and baskets of gold!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the real point of the ברייתא quoted in Steps 2-4
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that all מנחות are in a כלי שרת from start to finish
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the מנחה starts out in ordinary silver and gold baskets, which are not service vessels.

steps.title: רב פפא: vessels fit to become service vessels
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the משנה does not mean actual service vessels. It means vessels made of material, like silver and gold, that could become a כלי שרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Read the משנה as saying the מנחות are in vessels that are fit to be service vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge by explaining the משנה's words in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's words 'in a כלי שרת' are now read as 'in a vessel fit to be a כלי שרת.' Silver and gold baskets are fit, so the ברייתא and the משנה agree. The סוטה's מנחה is different because it is not brought in such a vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: Say / read it as (introduces a new reading of a text)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Read it as: in vessels
that are fit to be service vessels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 5
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה means actual service vessels, which contradicts the ordinary baskets in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means vessels fit to become service vessels, like silver and gold ones.

steps.title: So a cheap basket is not fit; whose view is that?
steps.stepSummary: From רב פפא's answer, the גמרא infers that a cheap Egyptian basket cannot be a כלי שרת. That seems to go against רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who allows wooden service vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that an Egyptian wicker basket is not fit to be a service vessel. Whose view is that? It is not the view of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. A ברייתא teaches: if service vessels were made of wood, רבי says they are not valid, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says they are valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from רב פפא's answer and asks which תנא that conclusion fits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סוטה's מנחה is set apart from the other מנחות because it comes in an Egyptian basket. That implies such a basket is not fit to be a כלי שרת. But רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה allows wooden service vessels, so the משנה seems to follow only רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication, from this we learn
An Egyptian wicker basket, a cheap basket woven from palm leaves

phrases.english: This implies that an Egyptian wicker basket is not fit,

phrases.aramaic: כְּמַאן — דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: whose view is that? Not the view of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: כְּלֵי שָׁרֵת שֶׁעֲשָׂאָן שֶׁל עֵץ,
phrases.english: as a ברייתא teaches: service vessels that one made of wood,
Rabbi says they are not valid,
phrases.notes: "רבי" by itself means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says they are valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלַל דִּכְפִיפָה מִצְרִית לָא חַזְיָא, כְּמַאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from רב פפא's answer and asks which תנא it fits
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה as explained by רב פפא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a cheap basket cannot be a service vessel, the משנה seems to go against רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who allows wooden service vessels.

steps.title: Even רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה rejects cheap vessels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה can match רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה too. He allows only valuable wooden vessels, not cheap ones, because of the פסוק 'Present it now to your governor.'
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. He said wooden vessels are valid when they are valuable. Did he say so about cheap ones? Doesn't רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה accept the פסוק 'Present it now to your governor'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the משנה does not have to go against רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה allows wood only for fine, valuable vessels. A cheap palm basket is something you would never present to a ruler. Since the פסוק teaches that what is unfit for a governor is unfit for the בית המקדש, even he would not allow it.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say (the source matches this opinion too)
"Present it now to your governor" (מלאכי 1:8): what you wouldn't give a ruler, don't bring to the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: Even the opinion that allows wooden service vessels allows only fine ones. Something cheap that you would be embarrassed to give a ruler can never be used in the בית המקדש.

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: You can even say it follows Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.aramaic: אֵימַר דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּחֲשׁוּבִין,
phrases.english: Granted, Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda said this about valuable vessels;
but did he say it about cheap ones?

phrases.aramaic: לֵית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: Doesn't Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda accept
"Present it now to your governor"?!
phrases.notes: מלאכי 1:8

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה allows any wooden vessel, so he would allow a cheap basket too.
steps.terutzMaskana: He allows only valuable wooden vessels. Cheap ones are ruled out by the פסוק in מלאכי.

steps.title: Does a service vessel make things holy only with intention?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא's words 'he puts it into a כלי שרת and makes it holy in a כלי שרת.' It asks whether this double wording teaches that a כלי שרת makes its contents holy only when the person intends it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: 'He puts it into a service vessel, and makes it holy in a service vessel.' Can we learn from this that service vessels make their contents holy only with intention?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new detail in the ברייתא and asks what its extra wording teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא could have just said 'he puts it into a כלי שרת.' Adding 'and makes it holy' sounds like a separate act, like intending to make it holy. So the גמרא asks whether a כלי שרת works only with intention.

phrases.english: "And he puts it into a service vessel,
and makes it holy in a service vessel."
Can you learn from this

phrases.aramaic: כְּלִי שָׁרֵת אֵין מְקַדְּשִׁין אֶלָּא מִדַּעַת?
phrases.english: that service vessels make things holy only with intention?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to a phrase of the ברייתא quoted in Step 2: the owner putting the מנחה into a כלי שרת
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the double wording teaches that a כלי שרת makes things holy only when the person intends it

steps.title: No: he puts it in so the vessel will make it holy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the ברייתא as one idea: he puts it into the כלי שרת so that the vessel will make it holy. The words do not require special intention.
steps.simpleTranslation: Read it as: he puts it into a service vessel in order to make it holy in the service vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא's wording does not teach that intention is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two phrases are not two separate acts. The second phrase just explains the purpose of the first: putting it in the vessel is what makes it holy. So there is no proof that a כלי שרת works only with intention.

keyTerms.meaning: In order to make it holy
In order to (the prefix that joins the two phrases into one idea)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's words 'and makes it holy' do not prove that a כלי שרת needs intention. They describe the purpose of putting the מנחה into the vessel.

phrases.english: Read it as: he puts it into a service vessel
in order to make it holy in the service vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: נוֹתְנָהּ בִּכְלִי שָׁרֵת לְקַדְּשָׁהּ בִּכְלִי שָׁרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The wording means he puts it in so that the vessel will make it holy. It does not prove that intention is needed.

steps.title: Putting oil and frankincense on the meal-offering
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the owner puts oil and לבונה on the מנחה, and the גמרא gives the פסוק this comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: He puts its oil and its frankincense on it, as the פסוק says: 'And he shall pour oil on it and put frankincense on it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes on to the next line of the ברייתא and shows which פסוק it comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is being challenged here. The ברייתא lists the steps of bringing a מנחה, and the גמרא simply gives each step its source. This step about oil and לבונה comes right after the step of putting the flour into a כלי שרת.

keyTerms.meaning: Oil, poured onto the flour of the מנחה
Frankincense, put on top of the מנחה
As it is said (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: And he puts on it its oil and its frankincense,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the מנחה. The person bringing it does this step, not the כהן yet.

phrases.english: as it is said: 'And he shall pour oil on it
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:1

phrases.english: and put frankincense on it.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the side discussion about כלי שרת, the גמרא goes back to reading the ברייתא's list of steps in order.
steps.raayaObject: The ברייתא's rule that the owner puts oil and לבונה on the מנחה
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 2:1: וְיָצַק עָלֶיהָ שֶׁמֶן וְנָתַן עָלֶיהָ לְבֹנָה

steps.title: Bringing the meal-offering to the כהן
steps.stepSummary: The owner carries the מנחה to a כהן, as the פסוק says, 'And he shall bring it to the sons of אהרן.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And he carries it to the כהן, as it is written: 'And he shall bring it to the sons of אהרן, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next step in the ברייתא and gives its פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the owner has done the work. Here the מנחה passes from the owner to the כהן, and the פסוק's words 'the sons of אהרן' are the source for bringing it to a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: The sons of אהרן, meaning the כהנים

phrases.english: And he carries it to the כהן,
as it is written: 'And he shall bring it to the sons of אהרן, etc.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:2. The 'etc.' means the פסוק keeps going: 'the כהנים'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next step in the same list, with its own פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: The ברייתא's rule that the owner brings the מנחה to the כהן

steps.title: The כהן brings it to the altar
steps.stepSummary: The כהן carries the מנחה to the מזבח, as the פסוק says, 'And he shall bring it near the altar.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And the כהן carries it to the מזבח, as it is written: 'And he shall bring it near to the altar.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the פסוק for the next step: the כהן takes the מנחה over to the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וְהִגִּישָׁהּ ('bring it near') is the source for the step called הגשה. This step leads into the next question, which asks exactly where on the מזבח the הגשה is done.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall bring it near
The step of bringing the מנחה up close to the מזבח

phrases.english: And the כהן carries it to the altar,
as it is written: 'And he shall bring it near to the altar.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:8

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next step in the list: the מנחה goes from the כהן's hands to the מזבח.
steps.raayaObject: The ברייתא's rule that the כהן brings the מנחה to the מזבח

steps.title: Where do we learn the southwest corner?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the כהן brings the מנחה to the southwest קרן of the מזבח, opposite the point of the corner, and that this is enough. The גמרא asks where we learn this.
steps.simpleTranslation: He brings it near at the southwest corner, opposite the point of the corner, and that is enough. From where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next detail in the ברייתא and asks for its source. This is a setup; the next step gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps each came with a פסוק right away. This detail is much more exact: a specific corner, the very point of that corner, and 'that is enough'. No פסוק says this openly, so the גמרא asks מנלן. It is not attacking the ברייתא; it wants to know the source.

keyTerms.meaning: The southwest corner of the מזבח
The sharp point or edge of the corner
From where do we know this?

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the question is left unanswered. The line ends with a dash because the answer follows right away in the next step.

phrases.english: He brings it near at the southwest corner
opposite the point of the corner, and that is enough.
From where do we derive this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 13 gave a source for bringing the מנחה to the מזבח. Now the גמרא asks for a source for the exact spot.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק teaches that הגשה is done at the southwest corner, opposite its point, and that this is enough.

steps.title: The source is the פסוק in the law of the מנחה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the question from step 14 by quoting the פסוק that says the מנחה is brought 'before ה׳, in front of the מזבח'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And this is the law of the מנחה: the sons of אהרן shall offer it before ה׳, in front of the מזבח.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the פסוק that is the source for where the מנחה is brought. The פסוק has two location phrases, and the next step shows how they work together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names two places: 'לפני ה׳' and 'אל פני המזבח'. On their own these seem to point in different directions. The ברייתא in the next step explains how to keep both.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written; this introduces a פסוק

phrases.english: As it is written: "And this is the law of the meal-offering:
the sons of Aaron shall offer it
before the Lord, in front of the altar"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14 by giving the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'לפני ה׳ אל פני המזבח' is the source for the location of the הגשה.

steps.title: The ברייתא keeps both phrases by using the southwest corner
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says 'לפני ה׳' alone would mean the west and 'אל פני המזבח' alone would mean the south. So the כהן brings the מנחה to the southwest corner, opposite its point, and that is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: 'Before ה׳': I might think on the west side, so the פסוק says 'in front of the מזבח'. If only 'in front of the מזבח', I might think on the south side, so the פסוק says 'before ה׳'. How so? He brings it near at the southwest corner, opposite the point of the corner, and that is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא reads the two phrases of the פסוק against each other. It concludes that the southwest corner fits both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase alone would limit the place to one side: west for 'לפני ה׳' and south for 'אל פני המזבח'. The corner where the west and south sides meet keeps both phrases. This is the exact ruling that step 14 asked about.

keyTerms.meaning: I might have thought; this opens a wrong first reading
The פסוק teaches; this brings the words that correct the first reading
How can this be? This brings the solution that fits both
The sharp point of the corner

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the two phrases argue with each other. The ברייתא uses each phrase to stop the other from being read too narrowly.

phrases.english: And it is taught in a baraita: "Before the Lord,"
I might have thought it means on the western side
therefore the verse says: "In front of the altar."
If it said only "in front of the altar,"
I might have thought it means on the southern side
therefore the verse says: "Before the Lord."
How so?
He brings it near at the southwest corner
opposite the point of the corner, and that is enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the פסוק from step 15 produces the southwest corner rule.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the מנחה is brought to the southwest corner.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading 'לפני ה׳' and 'אל פני המזבח' together.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: the south side of the corner is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר uses a rule: when one reading keeps both verses and another cancels one of them, choose the one that keeps both. Saying 'south' also keeps 'לפני ה׳', so the כהן brings the מנחה to the south side of the corner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: I might think he brings it to the west side of the corner or to the south side. Say: whenever you find two verses, where one keeps itself and the other, and one keeps itself but cancels the other, leave the one that cancels and take the one that keeps both. If 'before ה׳' means the west, you cancel 'in front of the מזבח' in the south. If 'in front of the מזבח' means the south, you also keep 'before ה׳' in the west. So he brings it to the south side of the corner.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives a different way to read the same פסוק. He uses a general rule about two verses that seem to clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא used the corner itself, where west and south meet. רבי אלעזר says the west reading would cancel the south, but the south reading still fits 'לפני ה׳'. So the south side of the corner is the right place.

keyTerms.meaning: Keeps its own meaning and also keeps the meaning of the other verse

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general tool for reading verses: when two verses seem to clash, choose the reading that leaves both with a meaning.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
I might have thought he brings it near on the western side of the corner
or on the southern side of the corner

phrases.aramaic: אָמַרְתָּ: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁאַתָּה מוֹצֵא שְׁנֵי מִקְרָאוֹת,
phrases.english: Say: anywhere you find two verses,

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד מְקַיֵּים עַצְמוֹ וּמְקַיֵּים דִּבְרֵי חֲבֵירוֹ,
phrases.english: one that fulfills itself and fulfills the words of the other,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶחָד מְקַיֵּים עַצְמוֹ וּמְבַטֵּל דִּבְרֵי חֲבֵירוֹ —
phrases.english: and one that fulfills itself and cancels the words of the other

phrases.aramaic: מַנִּיחִין אֶת שֶׁמְּקַיֵּים עַצְמוֹ וּמְבַטֵּל חֲבֵירוֹ,
phrases.english: we leave the one that fulfills itself and cancels the other,

phrases.aramaic: וְתוֹפְסִין אֶת שֶׁמְּקַיֵּים עַצְמוֹ וּמְקַיֵּים חֲבֵירוֹ.
phrases.english: and take hold of the one that fulfills itself and fulfills the other.
When you say "before the Lord" means the west,
you have canceled "in front of the altar," meaning the south,
but when you say "in front of the altar" means the south,
you have also fulfilled "before the Lord" in the west.

phrases.aramaic: הָא כֵּיצַד? מַגִּישָׁהּ לִדְרוֹמָהּ שֶׁל קֶרֶן.
phrases.english: How so? He brings it near on the southern side of the corner.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: יָכוֹל יַגִּישֶׁנָּה בְּמַעֲרָבָהּ שֶׁל קֶרֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second reading of the same פסוק that is different from the ברייתא in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Using the rule of two verses, the מנחה is brought to the south side of the corner.

steps.title: How does the south side keep 'לפני ה׳'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how bringing the מנחה to the south side still keeps 'לפני ה׳', which points west.
steps.simpleTranslation: But where did you keep 'before ה׳'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבי אלעזר's claim that the south reading also keeps 'לפני ה׳'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר said the south reading keeps both phrases. But the south side is not the west, so it is not clear how 'לפני ה׳' is kept. The next step answers this.

phrases.english: But where have you fulfilled it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the claim in step 17 that the south reading also keeps 'לפני ה׳'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the south side of the מזבח can count as 'לפני ה׳'.

steps.title: רב אשי: this תנא holds the whole מזבח is in the north
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says this תנא holds that the whole מזבח stands in the northern half of the עזרה. So even its south side still faces the west and counts as 'לפני ה׳'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: this תנא holds that the whole מזבח stands in the north.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains how the south side of the מזבח can still be 'לפני ה׳'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the whole מזבח is in the northern half of the עזרה, its south side still lines up with the היכל in the west. So bringing the מנחה to the south side also counts as 'לפני ה׳'.

keyTerms.meaning: A teacher from the time of the משנה

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
This tanna holds
that the entire altar stands in the north.
phrases.notes: He means the northern half of the עזרה, so even the altar's south side still lines up with the היכל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: קָסָבַר הַאי תַּנָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because the whole מזבח is in the north, its south side is still opposite the west, which is 'לפני ה׳'.

steps.title: What does 'ודיו' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא teaches with the word 'ודיו' ('and that is enough').
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'and that is enough' teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא from step 16 and asks why it added the word 'ודיו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא could have ended after giving the place. The word 'ודיו' seems to teach something extra, and the גמרא asks what that is.

phrases.english: What is meant by "and that is enough"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back from רבי אלעזר's approach to a word in the ברייתא of step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of the word 'ודיו' in the ברייתא.

steps.title: רב אשי: the מנחה does not need to touch the corner itself
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says 'ודיו' was needed. Otherwise we might think the מנחה itself must be brought up to the corner. It teaches that bringing it near in its vessel is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: it was needed. You might have thought the מנחה itself must be brought near. So the ברייתא teaches us that this is not needed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains that 'ודיו' tells us we do not need to bring the bare מנחה to the corner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without 'ודיו', we might have required the מנחה itself, out of its vessel, to be brought to the corner. 'ודיו' teaches that bringing it there inside the כלי שרת is enough. This connects to step 2, where the owner put the מנחה into the כלי שרת.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought to say

steps.whatToRemember: The הגשה of a מנחה is at the southwest corner of the מזבח (according to רבי אלעזר, its south side). It is done with the מנחה in its כלי שרת, and that is enough.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: It was necessary,
because it might enter your mind to say:
the meal-offering itself should need to be brought near,
so it teaches us that this is not so.
phrases.notes: Bringing it near while it is still in its vessel is enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אִיצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'ודיו' teaches that the מנחה does not have to be brought to the corner itself; bringing it near in its vessel is enough.

steps.title: Why not say the מנחה itself must touch the corner?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on step 21: maybe the מנחה really must be brought up to the corner itself, and bringing it in its vessel is not enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why not say that this is indeed so?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that bringing the מנחה near in its vessel is enough. It suggests that maybe the מנחה itself really must be brought up to the corner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 21, רב אשי said 'ודיו' teaches that bringing the מנחה in its vessel is enough. Now the גמרא asks why we shouldn't accept the opposite idea, the one 'ודיו' was said to reject. The גמרא wants a source showing that a vessel is truly fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Indeed so; it really is that way

phrases.english: And say that it is indeed so?
phrases.notes: He means: maybe the מנחה really should be brought up to the corner itself, not just in its vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of 'ודיו' given in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that 'ודיו' teaches that bringing the מנחה in its vessel is enough.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Why not say the rejected idea is actually correct, and the מנחה itself must be brought to the corner?

steps.title: A פסוק shows the מנחה is brought to the מזבח in a vessel
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק links bringing the מנחה to the כהן with bringing it to the מזבח. Just as the first is done in a vessel, so is the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And it shall be brought to the כהן... and he shall bring it near to the מזבח.' Just as bringing it to the כהן is done in a vessel, so too bringing it near to the מזבח is done in a vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. It compares bringing the מנחה to the מזבח with bringing it to the כהן, and both are done in a vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts 'והקריבה אל הכהן' and 'והגישה אל המזבח' side by side. Everyone agrees the מנחה is handed to the כהן inside a vessel. So the הגשה at the מזבח is also done in a vessel, and 'ודיו' stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Bringing the מנחה to the כהן
Bringing the מנחה near to the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: The הגשה at the מזבח is done with the מנחה still in its vessel, just like handing it to the כהן.

phrases.english: The verse says:
"And it shall be brought to the priest, etc.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:8

phrases.english: and he shall bring it near to the altar" —
just as bringing it to the priest is in a vessel,
so too bringing it near to the altar is in a vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22 with a פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural comparison (placing two acts side by side in one פסוק)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מנחה itself must be brought up to the corner of the מזבח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק compares הגשה with הקרבה to the כהן, so the הגשה is done in a vessel.

steps.title: The לבונה is moved to one side
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the כהן moves the לבונה to one side. The גמרא explains this is so none of it gets taken along with the flour in the קמיצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he moves its frankincense to one side, so that he does not take a handful of it together with the מנחה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא and gives the reason for it. The לבונה is pushed aside so it won't end up in the כהן's handful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קומץ must be taken from the flour of the מנחה. If the לבונה stayed mixed in, some of it could end up in the handful. Moving it aside keeps the קומץ clean.

phrases.english: And he moves its frankincense to one side.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלָא תִּקְּמוֹץ בַּהֲדֵי מִנְחָה,
phrases.english: So that it is not taken in the handful along with the meal-offering,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The לבונה is moved aside so that none of it is taken in the קמיצה.

steps.title: A משנה shows a קומץ with לבונה in it is פסול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: if a pebble, a grain of salt, or a bit of לבונה came up in the handful, the קמיצה is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: If he took the handful and a pebble, a grain of salt, or a crumb of frankincense came up in his hand, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports the reason it just gave with a משנה. Any foreign bit in the קומץ, including לבונה, makes it פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows why moving the לבונה aside matters. If even a crumb of לבונה gets into the handful, the קמיצה is ruined. So the כהן clears it away first.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the קומץ must be only the מנחה itself, with nothing else mixed in.

phrases.english: As we learned: If he took the handful and a pebble came up in his hand,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מנחות 6a.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ גַּרְגֵּר מֶלַח אוֹ קוֹרֶט לְבוֹנָה — פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: or a grain of salt, or a crumb of frankincense — it is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the reason given in step 24.
steps.raayaObject: The reason for moving the לבונה aside.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מנחות: a קומץ containing a crumb of לבונה is פסול.

steps.title: The קומץ is taken from where the oil collected
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the כהן takes the handful from the spot where most of the oil gathered.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he takes the handful from the place where its oil is plentiful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא. It is setting up a question about where this rule comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oil isn't spread evenly through the מנחה. The ברייתא says the כהן takes the קומץ from the oiliest spot. The next step asks for the source.

phrases.english: And he takes the handful from the place where its oil is plentiful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קמיצה is taken from the spot with the most oil.

steps.title: Where do we learn this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of taking the קומץ from the oily spot.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for the rule just quoted. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a request for a source, not an attack. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for taking the קומץ from the oily spot.

steps.title: Two פסוקים mention flour together with oil
steps.stepSummary: The פסוקים say 'from its flour and from its oil' and 'from its groats and from its oil.' So the handful should include plenty of oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'from its fine flour and from its oil,' and 'from its groats and from its oil.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with two פסוקים. Both mention oil alongside the flour that goes into the handful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the תורה says the קומץ is 'from its flour and from its oil,' the handful should contain oil too. Taking it from where the oil collected makes sure of that.

phrases.english: As it is written: "from its fine flour and from its oil,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:2

phrases.english: "from its groats and from its oil."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:16

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוקים pair the flour with its oil, so the קומץ is taken where the oil is plentiful.

steps.title: The קומץ is put in a כלי שרת to make it holy
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the כהן puts the קומץ into a כלי שרת and makes it holy there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he puts it into a service vessel and sanctifies it in the service vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא. It is setting up a question about why this is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the קמיצה, the handful goes into a כלי שרת, and that makes it holy. The next step asks why it needs to be made holy here at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A vessel used for the עבודה in the מקדש

phrases.english: And he puts it into a service vessel
and sanctifies it in the service vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קומץ is placed in a כלי שרת and is made holy there.

steps.title: Why make it holy again?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the קומץ needs to be made holy, since the מנחה was already made holy once.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need this? He already sanctified it once!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. If the מנחה was already made holy, why make it holy a second time?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מנחה was already made holy earlier, when it was placed in a כלי שרת. So a second קידוש seems unnecessary. The גמרא wants to know what it adds.

phrases.aramaic: לְמָה לִי? הָא קַדְּשַׁהּ חֲדָא זִימְנָא!
phrases.english: Why do I need this? He already sanctified it once!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the line quoted in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's requirement to make the קומץ holy in a כלי שרת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It was already made holy once, so a second קידוש seems pointless.

steps.title: Just like blood, which is made holy twice
steps.stepSummary: Blood is made holy by the knife at the animal's neck, yet it is made holy again in a כלי שרת. The קומץ is the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is just like blood. Even though the knife at the animal's neck made the blood holy, it is made holy again in a service vessel. Here too, it is no different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by comparing the קומץ to the blood of a קרבן. Blood is also made holy twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The knife is a כלי שרת, so the blood is made holy when the animal is slaughtered. Still, the blood is collected in a כלי שרת and made holy again. In the same way, the קומץ gets a second קידוש even though the מנחה was already holy.

keyTerms.meaning: The knife, which is itself a כלי שרת

steps.whatToRemember: A second קידוש in a כלי שרת is normal. Blood gets one too, after the knife has already made it holy.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the second קידוש means the first one didn't work. Both count; the עבודה simply includes a second קידוש, just as it does with blood.

phrases.english: It is just like blood;
blood, even though it was sanctified by
the knife at the animal's neck,
phrases.notes: The knife is a holy vessel, so it already makes the blood holy as the animal is slaughtered.

phrases.english: he sanctifies it again in a service vessel,
here too, it is no different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison to a known parallel (blood of a קרבן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One קידוש should be enough, so the second is pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: Like blood, which the knife makes holy and is then made holy again in a כלי שרת, the קומץ also gets a second קידוש.

steps.title: The כהן gathers the frankincense and puts it on the handful
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: the כהן collects the לבונה of the מנחה and places it on top of the קומץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he gathers its frankincense and puts it on top of the handful.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to its next step. After the קומץ is made holy, the כהן collects the לבונה and places it on top of the קומץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the ברייתא spoke only about the flour-and-oil handful. Now it adds the לבונה, which must be gathered up and placed on the קומץ so that the two go up together.

keyTerms.meaning: Frankincense, a fragrant spice placed on a מנחה
On top of it, meaning on top of the קומץ

phrases.english: And he gathers its frankincense
and puts it on top of it
phrases.notes: 'It' is the קומץ, the handful the כהן just made holy in the כלי שרת.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְלַקֵּט אֶת לְבוֹנָתָהּ וְנוֹתְנָהּ עַל גַּבָּיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's sequence after the קומץ is made holy in a כלי שרת (Steps 29–31).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן gathers all the לבונה and places it on top of the קומץ.

steps.title: The פסוק that teaches gathering all the frankincense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the source: the פסוק says 'and all the frankincense which is upon the מנחה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And all the frankincense which is upon the meal-offering.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where the rule of gathering the לבונה comes from. It quotes a פסוק about the מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists the לבונה together with the קומץ that the כהן takes up. That is why the כהן gathers the לבונה and places it on the קומץ, so they go up together.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written, introducing a פסוק

phrases.english: As it is written: "And all the frankincense
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:8

phrases.english: which is upon the meal-offering."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the scriptural source for the ruling in Step 32.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the כהן gathers the לבונה and puts it with the קומץ.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 6:8: 'and all the frankincense which is upon the meal-offering.'

steps.title: The ברייתא's next step: he brings it up
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא begins its next clause: the כהן brings up the קומץ with its לבונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he brings it up.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts its next step: the כהן brings up the קומץ together with the לבונה. This is a setup line, and the rest of this step continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that the קומץ and לבונה are together, the ברייתא moves to carrying them up. The amud ends on this word, so the details come on the next amud.

phrases.english: And he brings it up
phrases.notes: 'It' is the קומץ with the לבונה on top. The text right after this goes on with this step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's order of steps after the לבונה is placed on the קומץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After placing the לבונה on the קומץ, the כהן brings it up. The details continue in the next part of the text.
